newsitem.title: CANADA: Angry Bre-X investors may target brokerages.
newsitem.headline: Angry Bre-X investors may target brokerages.

text.p: Some embittered shareholders of Bre-X Minerals Ltd threatened on Monday to take aim at major Canadian banks and investment dealers over the massive mining scandal exposed late on Sunday.
A group representing about 200 Bre-X shareholders said in a statement that it recommended forming an association to retain lawyers for possible litigation against Canada's investment dealers.

"This body will mandate a Quebec, Ontario and B.C. (British Columbia) law firm to pursue all necessary, viable and appropriate legal actions against any and all parties who may have a liability resulting from their involvement in the Bre-X dossier," wrote Public Interest Research Associates spokesman, Dermod Travis.

Mining analysts at major Canadian banks declined to comment specifically on any investment industry culpability over the Bre-X gold find in Indonesia, described in a independent consulting report late on Sunday as a historically unprecedented fraud.

Traders said that shares of Bank of Montreal, Canada's third biggest bank, fell C$1.10 to C$52.25 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday amid rumors its investment arm Nesbitt Burns Inc would be a target of shareholder suits.
"They're going to sue the pants off Nesbitt. They're going to sue the pants off their broker. They're going to sue the pants off the guys at Bre-X," one equity trader said.
Nesbitt Burns President John MacNaughton said the brokerage community was startled by the Bre-X debacle.
"Like others around the world we have been startled to learn that the investment industry...has been victimized by fraudulent activities on an unprecedented and massive scale," MacNaughton said.

The Sunday report from independent mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd said the Bre-X Busang discovery in Indonesia -- touted by the Calgary, Alberta-based prospector as the richest find of the century -- was falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining."

Nesbitt's top mining analyst, Egizio Bianchini, considered one of the best in Canada, wrote that "the gold is there!" in a report shortly before news on March 26 that Bre-X's Busang partner Freeport McMoran Copper & Gold Inc. said preliminary tests found "insignificant" amounts of gold.
The news lopped almost C$3 billion ($2.1 billion) off Bre-X's market value as the stock plummeted to C$2.50 ($1.80) from around C$15 ($11).

"Prior to recommending a share, there is a certain amount of homework that an investment dealer is supposed to undertake and we are going to be most fascinated to see if that homework was done and was as comprehensive as is appropriate when you are making recommendations on investments that total in the hundreds of millions of dollars," said Travis of the shareholders group.
Bank of Nova Scotia said its brokerage arm, ScotiaMcLeod Inc, has had a sell recommendation on Bre-X since February 17.
"At this point we don't have anything further to add other than the facts that were released by Strathcona last night," said Donna Cox, spokeswoman for Bank of Nova Scotia.
The editor of an influential mining newsletter said Canada's brokerage houses should shoulder some of the blame for the Bre-X scandal.

"What analysts can be criticized for is that at some stage it became so big, they should have said, 'Wait Mr. Felderhof. Why don't you have somebody come in and do some independent verification just to be on the safe side,'" said John Kaiser, editor of the Kaiser Bottom-Fishing Report, referring to Bre-X's head of exploration.
